messages.subject: creating a simple pie chart
parts:
Hi,

I have a simple problem that I just cannot get - I need to create a
simple pie chart. My data frame is

data <- data.frame(cluster = paste("Cluster", 1:4), size =
c(0.5519, 0.2238, 0.1544, 0.0698))

where "size" is the proportion of consumers in each cluster (and sum to
1.0). The pie should have four slices, each the size of "size" and the
legend should simply be the cluster names from "cluster". How do I do
this????

Also, how do I get labels on the slices (e.g., "Cluster 1: 0.5519")?

Thanks,

Walt

messages.subject: Re: creating a simple pie chart
parts:
Walt,

following Hadley's example in the coord_polar help:

pie <- ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(1), fill = cluster, weight=size)) +
 geom_bar(width = 1) + coord_polar(theta="y")
pie

HTH,
Heike

parts:
Walt, 

It's not pretty, but I used geom_text() to put some labels on there. I had to hand edit the position in though, which means that you'd probably be better off with sigmaplot or Excel (*shudder*).

data <- data.frame(cluster = paste("Cluster", 1:4), size = c(0.5519, 0.2238, 0.1544, 0.0698), position = c(0.5519, 0.5519+0.2238, 0.5519+0.2238+0.1544, 0.5519+0.2238+0.1544+0.0698), position2 = c(0.3, 0.7, 0.85, 0.965))
ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(1), fill = cluster, weight=size)) +

geom_bar(width = 1) + geom_text(aes(y=position2, label=size))+coord_polar(theta="y")

Brandon

parts:
Sigmaplot/Excel was a joke on my part. 

The following code gives you a very stripped down pie. Looks pretty decent if you ask me.

data <- data.frame(cluster = paste("Cluster", 1:4), size = c(0.5519, 0.2238, 0.1544, 0.0698), position = c(0.5519, 0.5519+0.2238, 0.5519+0.2238+0.1544, 0.5519+0.2238+0.1544+0.0698), position2 = c(0.3, 0.7, 0.85, 0.965))

ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(1), fill = cluster, weight=size)) +

geom_bar(width = 1) + geom_text(aes(y=position2, label=size))+coord_polar(theta="y")+theme_bw() + opts(axis.title.x = theme_blank(), axis.title.y= theme_blank(), axis.text.x=theme_blank(), axis.text.y=theme_blank(), panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(), panel.grid.major = theme_blank(), panel.border = theme_blank())


I suppose the reason pie charts are so hard is that it's probably underutilized in everywhere but business (where it is overused IMO). With more use, more work will be put into it. Aside from the labels, I think we're getting pretty darn close don't you think Walt? 

Brandon

messages.subject: Re: creating a simple pie chart
parts:
The reason it probably can't be geom_pie() is that (as created in
this way) it's not really its own
geom, it's a geom_bar() in polar coordinates. geom_pie() would be
something closer to the floating.pie()
function in the plotrix package.
A reason to write a geom_pie() from scratch would be to enable
functionality like floating.pie (which is
used, for example in population genetics, to display breakdown of allele
proportions at different geographic locations).
This would have to have aesthetics x,y, (location on the plot) fill
(slice colours) colour (border colours), proportion (slice areas),
text (labels),size ... Writing new non-trivial geoms looks tricky
though, at least to me.

For what it's worth, there's a small counter-literature (the Spence
2005 reference <http://www.psych.utoronto.ca/users/spence/Spence%202005.pdf>
from the wikipedia 'pie chart' article is a starting point) that says
pie charts aren't that bad
(although Few <http://www.perceptualedge.com/articles/08-21-07.pdf>, who
tries to be pretty thorough,
finds only one small case where they're provably better).

There's something to be said for culture, too. I think the example
above from population genetics isn't
that bad -- I don't think you'd gain that much by re-doing them as bar
charts or stacked bars.

messages.subject: Re: creating a simple pie chart
parts: here is an excellent example ;-p

data <- data.frame(cluster = paste("Cluster", 1:4), size = c(0.5519,
0.2238, 0.1544, 0.0698))

data$p<-(p<-cumsum(data$size)-diff(c(0,cumsum(data$size)))*(1-0.5)) #
is this simplest?
ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(1), fill = cluster, weight=size)) +

geom_bar(width=1) + geom_text(aes(x= 1.6, y=p,
angle=-p*360,label=size),vjust=0)+coord_polar(theta="y")

- you can control the distance between pie and text by changing x=1.6
- you can control the position of the text along the pie by changing 1-0.5
- you can also control the angle of the text.
